- **IA Handoff For Codex**: Provided implementation-specific guidance, emphasizing "Sackjack First" priority and the use of absolute-style paths in the partials system to prevent broken assets during migration.

### Motivation
- Ensure bootstrap chest placement triggers a deterministic, immediate handoff for conversion setup instead of relying solely on ambient world scans or pairing callbacks.
- Make pairing effects (listener registration, furnace/crafting-table resolution, lifecycle reconciliation) explicit and reproducible after successful bootstrap chest placement.
- Emit structured logs for observability around the handoff and warn if the expected callback path does not complete within a configurable tick threshold.

### Description
- Added a new `LumberjackBehavior.runPostBootstrapHandoff(...)` API that: registers chest listeners, resolves paired crafting-table/furnace context, and invokes lifecycle reconciliation via `reconcileAndMaybeConvert(...)` (and records a pending callback entry when requested). The public entrypoint is `runPostBootstrapHandoff(ServerWorld, VillagerEntity, BlockPos, BlockPos)`.

- Introduced tracking for pending post-bootstrap callbacks via `PENDING_POST_BOOTSTRAP_CALLBACKS` and a tick threshold `POST_BOOTSTRAP_CALLBACK_WARN_TICKS = 100L` with a periodic check that emits `event=lumberjack_post_bootstrap_callback_missing` if no callback path is observed after the threshold.

author: jakeshaver
body:
## Problem

`make app` (and `make zip`) fails with:

```
ClaudeUsageBar.app: resource fork, Finder information, or similar detritus not allowed
```

This happens because `actool` and/or `ditto` can leave extended attributes (resource forks, Finder metadata, quarantine flags) on bundle files. `codesign` treats any such attributes as an error and refuses to sign.

Reproduces reliably when:
- Building on top of a bundle directory that was previously downloaded from the internet
- Running the build script more than once on the same output directory
- Building on macOS 15+

## Fix

Add `xattr -cr "$APP_BUNDLE"` immediately before the `codesign` step. This strips all extended attributes from the bundle tree and is the standard fix recommended in Apple's documentation and developer forums.

**One line change to `scripts/build.sh`.**

## Verification

```bash
make app   # previously failed; now succeeds cleanly
make zip   # end-to-end release build succeeds
```

Several platform features were missing or incomplete: the "Open to Work" badge was static, chat showed "connecting..." permanently, match notifications only fired at 100%, users couldn't manage their own skills/experiences, employers couldn't resign their role, company admins had no employer management UI, and employers weren't appearing in the company member list.

## IsOpenToWork Field

- Added `IsOpenToWork` (bool, default `true`) to `User` model + migration `20260307000001`
- Auto-set to `false` when employer request is approved (`ApproveEmployerRole`) or applicant accepts a final offer (`ApplicantRespond` Status 3→4)
- Users can toggle it themselves via Edit Profile switch or `PUT /api/users/{id}/open-to-work`
- `Details.cshtml` badge is now dynamic: 🟢 open · 💼 employed · 🏢 employer

## Employer Self-Management + Company Admin Controls

- `POST /api/users/me/resign-employer` — user resets own role to 1, clears company memberships, sets `IsOpenToWork=true`
- `GET/DELETE /api/users/company/{id}/employers` — list/remove active employers (CompanyAdmin or Admin)
- `GET /api/users/company/{id}/employer-requests` — pending employer requests scoped to company
- Companies `Edit.cshtml` now renders an employer list + pending requests panel with approve/reject actions (JS-driven, visible to Admin/Employer)

## Skill Validation Workflow

New `SkillValidationRequest` model + EF config. Users can either add existing skills directly or submit a new skill with a supporting document (PDF/image, ≤5MB):

```
POST /api/userskills/validation-request  (multipart: skillName, document, notes)
→ Status 0 (Pending) → Admin reviews → Status 1 (Approved, skill added) or 2 (Rejected)
→ Notifications: SkillValidationRequest (admins) / SkillValidationApproved|Rejected (user)
```

Admin endpoints: `GET /api/userskills/validation-requests` + `POST .../review`. Edit Profile page exposes the full skill + experience management UI via fetch calls.

`ValidateDocumentOrImageFile` added to `IFileStorageService` to allow PDFs alongside images.

## Chat Online Presence

`ChatHub` now tracks connections in `ConcurrentDictionary<int, HashSet<string>>` (supports multiple tabs):
- `OnConnected/Disconnected` broadcast `UserOnline` to all chats the user participates in
- `JoinChat` returns `ParticipantPresence` with current online state of other participants
- Chat UI handles these events; header now shows `🟢 Online` / `⚫ Offline` based on actual participant presence rather than SignalR connection state

## 90%+ Match Notifications

Changed `score == 100` → `score >= 90` in `NotifyPerfectMatchUsersAsync`. Notification type renamed `PerfectOpportunityMatch` → `HighMatchOpportunity`; payload now includes `matchScore`.

## README

Created `README.md` at repo root documenting architecture, authorization model, all API endpoints, business logic (match algorithm, pipeline stages, notification types), DB migrations, and key services.

## Explanation

This PR adds CEL expression support to the `issuer`, `subject`, `issuerRegExp`, and `subjectRegExp` fields of the `Identity` type in `ImageValidatingPolicy`'s keyless (Fulcio/Sigstore) configuration. Previously these fields only accepted static strings, which forced users to write one policy per image when they needed per-image signing identity pinning. With this change, each field accepts either a plain string (unchanged) or a `{expression: "..."}` CEL expression that is evaluated at admission time with full access to the request context — enabling a single policy to enforce precise per-image signing identities across an entire organization.

This is a backward-compatible addition: all existing policies using plain string values continue to work without modification.

## Related issue

Fixes https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/issues/15398
Depend on https://github.com/kyverno/api/pull/64

<!--
Closes #<issue-number>
-->

## Milestone of this PR

<!--
Add the milestone label by commenting `/milestone 1.2.3`.
-->

## Documentation (required for features)

My PR contains new or altered behavior to Kyverno.
- [ ] I have sent the draft PR to add or update [the documentation](https://github.com/kyverno/website) and the link is:

## What type of PR is this

/kind api-change
/kind feature

## Proposed Changes

The `Identity` struct fields (`issuer`, `subject`, `issuerRegExp`, `subjectRegExp`) are changed from plain `string` to `*StringOrExpression` — the same union type already used for `cert`, `certChain`, and Notary `certs` fields. A custom `UnmarshalJSON` on `StringOrExpression` ensures that a plain YAML string (e.g. `issuer: "https://..."`) is transparently decoded into `StringOrExpression{Value: "..."}`, so no existing policies need to be updated.

At policy compile time, any `{expression: "..."}` values are compiled into CEL programs. At admission time, those programs are evaluated against the full request context (including `object`, `images`, `request`, and `variables`) and their string results are substituted as the identity values passed to cosign's `CheckOpts.Identities`. This means `subject` and `subjectRegExp` are matched against the Fulcio certificate's SAN URI, and `issuer`/`issuerRegExp` against the OIDC issuer OID extension, exactly as before — the only difference is the values can now be computed rather than hardcoded.

Changes:
- `api/policies.kyverno.io/v1alpha1/imagevalidating_policy.go` — change `Identity`
  fields to `*StringOrExpression`; add backward-compatible `UnmarshalJSON` on
  `StringOrExpression`
- `api/policies.kyverno.io/v1alpha1/zz_generated.deepcopy.go` — update
  `Identity.DeepCopyInto` and `Keyless.DeepCopyInto` for the new pointer fields
- `pkg/imageverification/variables/attestors.go` — compile and evaluate CEL expressions
  for identity fields
- `pkg/imageverification/imageverifiers/cosign/opts.go` — read `.Value` from pointer
  fields when building `cosign.CheckOpts`

### Proof Manifests

#### Example 1: Backward-compatible plain string (no change needed)

Existing policies continue to work unchanged:

```yaml
apiVersion: policies.kyverno.io/v1alpha1
kind: ImageValidatingPolicy
metadata:
  name: verify-image-keyless-static
spec:
  failurePolicy: Fail
  validationActions:
    - Deny
  matchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
      - apiGroups: [""]
        apiVersions: ["v1"]
        operations: ["CREATE", "UPDATE"]
        resources: ["pods"]
  attestors:
    - name: sigstore
      cosign:
        keyless:
          identities:
            - issuer: "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com"
              subject: "https://github.com/my-org/my-repo/.github/workflows/release.yml@refs/heads/main"
  validations:
    - expression: >-
        images.containers.map(image, verifyImageSignatures(image, [attestors.sigstore])).all(e, e > 0)
      message: Image signature verification failed.
```

#### Example 2: Derive subject from a pod label (per-repo identity, one policy for all services)

The expected signer workflow is derived from the `github-repo` pod label at admission
time. `subject` and `subjectRegExp` match against the Fulcio certificate's SAN URI;
`issuer`/`issuerRegExp` match against the OIDC issuer OID extension on the certificate.

```yaml
apiVersion: policies.kyverno.io/v1alpha1
kind: ImageValidatingPolicy
metadata:
  name: verify-image-keyless-cel-identity
spec:
  failurePolicy: Fail
  validationActions:
    - Deny
  matchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
      - apiGroups: [""]
        apiVersions: ["v1"]
        operations: ["CREATE", "UPDATE"]
        resources: ["pods"]
  attestors:
    - name: sigstore
      cosign:
        keyless:
          identities:
            - issuer:
                value: "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com"
              subject:
                expression: >-
                  "https://github.com/" + object.metadata.labels["github-repo"] +
                  "/.github/workflows/release.yml@refs/heads/main"
  validations:
    - expression: >-
        images.containers.map(image, verifyImageSignatures(image, [attestors.sigstore])).all(e, e > 0)
      message: >-
        Image signature verification failed. The image must be signed by the
        GitHub Actions workflow for the repository specified in the 'github-repo' label.
```

```yaml

kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: my-app
  labels:
    github-repo: "my-org/my-app"
spec:
  containers:
    - name: app
      image: ghcr.io/my-org/my-app:v1.2.3
```

Pod that is denied (label does not match the actual signing identity):

```yaml

kind: Pod
metadata:
```

author: mmcky
body:
## Summary

Fix compatibility with `myst-nb` 1.4.0+ by setting the `data-theme` attribute, increasing CSS specificity for custom syntax highlighting, adding a configurable `inline_literal_box` option, and integrating inline code literal color into the text color scheme system.

## Problem

`myst-nb` 1.4.0 ([executablebooks/MyST-NB#693](https://github.com/executablebooks/MyST-NB/pull/693)) changed its CSS dark mode detection from `html[data-theme="dark"]` selectors to a [CSS space-toggle technique](https://lea.verou.me/blog/2020/10/the-var-space-hack-to-toggle-multiple-values-with-one-custom-property/) with `@media (prefers-color-scheme)` fallback. Since `quantecon-book-theme` uses `body.dark-theme` class for dark mode (not `data-theme` attribute), `myst-nb` never detects the theme's mode and falls through to the OS color scheme preference — causing dark code cell backgrounds on a light-themed site.

This was temporarily worked around by pinning `myst-nb<1.4.0` in downstream projects (see [QuantEcon/lecture-python.myst#825](https://github.com/QuantEcon/lecture-python.myst/pull/825)).

## Changes

### 1. Set `data-theme` on `<html>` (the standard signal)

Set `data-theme` on `<html>` (the standard signal used by pydata-sphinx-theme, Furo, and sphinx-book-theme) in three places:

1. **`layout.html` early script** — sets `data-theme="light"` by default, or `"dark"` if dark mode was previously saved, preventing flash of incorrect styles
2. **`theme-settings.js` `setContrast()`** — syncs `data-theme` on page load
3. **`theme-settings.js` click handler** — toggles `data-theme` when the contrast button is clicked

The existing `body.dark-theme` class mechanism is preserved for backward compatibility.

### 2. Increase CSS specificity for custom code highlighting

Setting `data-theme` activated pydata-sphinx-theme's Pygments CSS rules, which are all scoped to `html[data-theme="light/dark"] .highlight` (specificity `(0,3,1)`). Our custom highlighting in `_code.scss` and `_syntax.scss` used `:where()` for zero specificity, so pydata's rules overrode all our custom token colors.

**Fix**: Replaced `:where(body:not(.use-pygments-style))` with `html body:not(.use-pygments-style)` giving specificity `(0,3,2)` — beating pydata's `(0,3,1)`.

### 3. Add `inline_literal_box` option

`pydata-sphinx-theme` applies background, border, and padding to `code.literal` elements. A new theme option controls this:

- **`inline_literal_box: False`** (default) — strips the box styling to match our original look
- **`inline_literal_box: True`** — re-enables pydata's box/border/padding on inline code

```python
html_theme_options = {
    "inline_literal_box": True,  # enable inline code boxes
}
```

### 4. Add `--qe-literal-color` to text color scheme system

Integrated inline code literal (`code.literal`) color into the color scheme system alongside emphasis, strong, and definition colors:

| Scheme | Light Mode | Dark Mode |
|---|---|---|
| **seoul256** (default) | `#af5f5f` muted rust | `#d78787` soft rose |
| **gruvbox** | `#9d0006` dark red | `#fb4934` bright red |
| **none** | inherits text color | inherits text color |

Overridable via `--qe-literal-color` CSS variable in a custom stylesheet.

## Files Changed

- **`layout.html`** — `data-theme` in flash-prevention script + `inline-literal-box` body class
- **`theme-settings.js`** — `data-theme` sync in `setContrast()` and click handler
- **`_code.scss`** — CSS specificity fix + `code.literal` box override
- **`_syntax.scss`** — CSS specificity fix
- **`_colors.scss`** — Seoul256 and Gruvbox literal color variables
- **`_base.scss`** — `code.literal` color rule
- **`_dark-theme.scss`** — dark mode `code.literal` color
- **`_color-schemes.scss`** — gruvbox and none scheme literal rules
- **`theme.conf`** — `inline_literal_box` option
- **`__init__.py`** — `inline_literal_box` context variable
- **`code-highlighting.md`** — inline code box + color documentation
- **`text-color-schemes.md`** — literal color in scheme tables and examples

- Webpack build succeeds (`npm run build`)
- Visual snapshots need regeneration (`/update-snapshots`)

author: toldandretold
body:
Adds ability to hyperlight/footnote within a hyperlight/footnote

This depends on a change whereby footnote and hyperlight content is treated as any other book... and so its content is stored in the nodes column.

However, the first five nodes are stored also in the footnotes/hyperlights tables as "preview_nodes". Thus, each book loads along with all the relevant hyperlights/footnotes to show when a user clicks them.

Then, when a footnote/hyperlight is clicked, we pull the data for that footnote/hyperlight from backend as a book, and so we pull all its nodes, hyperlights and footnotes data too... and we do this step-by-step as user goes deeper and deeper into deeply nested nodes.

This took a lot of time, and there will likely be errors, because it requires making each footnote/hyperlight function the same as main-content, that means any pasting, hyperciting, edit toolbar, etc etc, has to be compatible with the active div on page.

* 🎯 **What:** The OAuth `state` parameter is now dynamically generated and validated upon the authentication redirect callback. Tests were updated and made deterministic by clearing function caches appropriately.
* ⚠️ **Risk:** A static state parameter leaves the application vulnerable to Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF). An attacker could forge a request linking a victim's session to the attacker's Whoop account or vice versa, compromising integration security.
* 🛡️ **Solution:** `whoop.py` generates a cryptographically secure random string using `secrets.token_urlsafe(16)` and sets it in `st.session_state.oauth_state`. During the callback flow in `app.py`, this state is retrieved and strictly validated against the URL `state` query parameter before exchanging the token. To prevent reuse, the session state variable is then deleted.

body:
Add two built-in function sorters for config.function_sorter
(from #200) to order functions by dependency in schema.rb:

- FunctionsSortByDependency: parses SQL definitions with regex
  to detect function calls. Works without a DB connection.
  Handles PL/pgSQL well since it scans function bodies
  directly. Strips comments and string literals to avoid false
  positives.
- FunctionsSortByPgDepend: queries PostgreSQL's pg_depend
  catalog for real dependency edges. Authoritative for
  SQL-language functions. Does not cover PL/pgSQL (PostgreSQL
  defers parsing to execution time).

Both use TSort with strongly_connected_components to tolerate
mutually recursive functions.

author: copilot
body:
This updates EV ranking policy from global EV sorting to prediction-first ordering: urgency horizon is now primary, with EV used to rank candidates *within* the same urgency class. The goal is to keep near-ready/liquidatable opportunities ahead of far-horizon high-EV names while preserving existing EV/TTL computation.

- **Ranking policy change (EV mode only)**
  - In `selectCandidates(...)`, candidates are assigned `rankBucket`:
    - `liquidatable`
    - `near-ready`
    - `medium-horizon`
    - `far-horizon`
    - `legacy-or-unknown`
  - Bucket classification follows required precedence and conditions (liquidatable/HR, near threshold or short TTL, medium TTL, pair-aware far, then legacy/unknown fallback).
  - Added `forecast.ttlMinutes` for comparator use.

- **Comparator rewrite (bucket-first)**
  - Replaced global EV sort with ordered comparator:
    1. bucket priority (asc)
    2. EV (desc)
    3. TTL minutes (asc, when both finite)
    4. health ratio (asc)
    5. priority score (desc)
    6. obligation pubkey (stable tie-break)
  - Non-EV mode behavior remains unchanged.

- **Snapshot diagnostics**
  - Added compact `Bucket` column in EV table output (`liq`, `near`, `mid`, `far`, `legacy`).
  - Added rank-bucket summary counts for top candidates.

- **Candidate validation policy**
  - Updated `scripts/validate_candidates.ts` EV-mode checks to enforce:
    - non-decreasing bucket priority
    - EV non-increasing within the same bucket
  - Kept existing structure/completeness checks.

- **Tests**
  - Added/updated ranking tests to cover:
    - near-ready lower-EV above far-horizon higher-EV
    - liquidatable always above non-liquidatable
    - legacy-global behind pair-aware in EV mode
    - EV-desc ordering inside the same bucket

```ts
// EV mode ordering policy
candidates
  .map(enrichWithForecastAndEv)
  .map((c) => ({ ...c, rankBucket: classifyRankBucket(c, nearThreshold, c.forecast?.ttlMinutes ?? null) }))
  .sort((a, b) =>
    bucketOrder(a) - bucketOrder(b) ||
    (b.ev ?? 0) - (a.ev ?? 0) ||
    ttlAscIfBothFinite(a, b) ||
    a.healthRatio - b.healthRatio ||
    b.priorityScore - a.priorityScore ||
    a.obligationPubkey.localeCompare(b.obligationPubkey)
  );
```

`exhibitorCounts` in `BookmarkCountsContext` was only refreshed by the Firestore sync load — toggling a bookmark fired an async Firestore write but left local React state stale, so the displayed counter didn't move until the next sync cycle.

## Changes

- **`BookmarkCountsContext`** — adds `adjustExhibitorCount(exhibitorId, delta: 1 | -1)` for optimistic local updates; clamps to `Math.max(0, ...)` and persists to localStorage

- **`FirebaseExhibitorBookmarkSync`** — calls `adjustExhibitorCount` synchronously for each added/removed exhibitor (diff against last saved snapshot) before the async Firestore write, giving immediate UI feedback

```ts
// Optimistically update local counts so the UI reflects the change immediately.
added.forEach((id) => adjustExhibitorCount(id, 1));
removed.forEach((id) => adjustExhibitorCount(id, -1));

// Then persist to Firestore as before
added.forEach((id) =>
  incrementExhibitorBookmarkCount(conferenceId, id, 1).catch(console.error),
);
```
